newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage market directionless before FOMC results.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage market directionless before FOMC results.

text.p: Mortgage-backed securities (MBS) were little changed at midday Tuesday before the Federal Open Market Committee meeting results.

Traders concurred the FOMC would leave rates unchanged. There was little else to give the markets direction, however. Ten-year U.S. Treasuries, which generally point the way for the mortgage market, were also unchanged in featureless trade.

In 30-year 7 1/2s, Freddie Macs were flat at 101-15/32 to yield 7.28 percent, Government National Mortgage Association bonds rose 1/32 to 101-10/32 to yield 7.33 percent and Fannie Maes dipped 1/32 to 101-16/32 to yield 7.23 percent.

News that July housing starts were flat at an annual rate of 1.447 million units did not sway MBS from narrow trading bands. A Reuters poll had predicted a slight rise. Still, several economists said recent indicators pointed to continued homebuilding strength through year-end and a peak of about 1.5 million units for the year.
Estimates about the prospects for faster MBS prepayments remained divided, pending further direction for Treasuries.
Michael Youngblood, managing director and head of mortgage research at Chase Securities Inc, said he was "not at all surprised to see a diversity of opinion" regarding prepays.

"The street has been systematically underestimating prepayments when they've increased this year," Youngblood said. "There is also the difficulty that analysts have with analyzing seasonal influences this late in the year. Prepayments are seasonally bound to the school year cycle."

He added that Chase "is in the bullish camp in regard to prepayments." Chase expects August prepays will accelerate at a faster pace than in July. "We further think that prepayments, particularly in the most vulnerable 7 1/2 percent to 8 1/2 percent coupons, will be as fast with a chance of being even faster in the month of September." (( -- Lynn Adler, U.S. Mortgage Unit, 212-859-1677 ))
